definition.title: Participate
definition.summary: Curated astronomy citizen-science opportunities, evergreen observing challenges, and reviewed hands-on activities with explicit safety and external-handoff boundaries.
definition.external_handoff_notice: You are leaving Lumina for Zooniverse. Zooniverse account, privacy, moderation, and community rules apply on the external site.
definition.privacy_note: Lumina does not send location, age, identity, challenge completion, activity completion, or Zooniverse account data to the Participate API.

projects.title: Galaxy Zoo
projects.summary: Classify galaxy images by visible shape and structure to support studies of galaxy evolution.
projects.time_label: About 10 minutes to learn the basics
projects.knowledge_note: No prior knowledge required; the project provides a tutorial and field guide.

projects.title: Planet Hunters TESS
projects.summary: Inspect TESS light curves for transit-like dips that may indicate orbiting exoplanets.
projects.knowledge_note: No prior knowledge required; the in-project tutorial and field guide provide instruction.

projects.title: The Daily Minor Planet
projects.summary: Review candidate asteroid image sequences and distinguish real moving objects from false detections.
projects.time_label: 5–15 minutes to complete the tutorial and field-guide familiarization
projects.knowledge_note: No prior knowledge required; an in-project tutorial provides the instruction.

projects.title: Redshift Wrangler
projects.summary: Inspect galaxy spectra for features and check automated spectral fits used to study galaxy redshift.
projects.knowledge_note: No prior knowledge required; the in-project tutorial provides the instruction.

projects.title: Active Asteroids
projects.summary: Search telescope images for asteroid-like objects showing comet-like activity such as tails or comae.
projects.time_label: A few minutes of in-project training
projects.knowledge_note: No prior knowledge required; in-project training is provided.

projects.title: Cloudspotting on Mars
projects.summary: Inspect graphed Mars Climate Sounder data and mark patterns associated with Martian clouds.
projects.knowledge_note: No prior knowledge required; in-project training is provided.

challenges.title: Moon journal
challenges.summary: Make four short Moon observations and record date, local time, visible shape, and observing conditions.
challenges.duration_label: Four short observations across the month
steps: On four safe observing opportunities, look for the Moon with unaided eyes.
Record date, local time, a simple shape sketch, and cloud/light conditions.
Compare the four entries without requiring a phase-name guess.
safety: Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: Clouds or an unavailable Moon are valid entries; record the limitation rather than inventing an observation.

challenges.title: Same-sky revisit
challenges.summary: Sketch one bright sky pattern on two separated nights and compare what appears unchanged or shifted.
steps: Choose one bright, easy-to-relocate patch of sky from a permitted place.
Make a simple dot-and-line sketch.
Repeat on another night from the same stationary place when practical and compare the sketches.
safety: Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: Identification is optional; a comparison of visible patterns is sufficient.

challenges.title: Changing shadow log
challenges.summary: Mark the tip of one stationary object's shadow three times and compare how it changes.
challenges.duration_label: Three daytime checks separated by at least 30 minutes
steps: Choose a stable upright object in a safe open place.
Without looking at the Sun, mark or sketch the shadow tip.
Repeat twice later and compare direction and length.
safety: Never stare at or deliberately look toward the Sun; observe only the shadow on the ground.
Keep the observation area clear of traffic and trip hazards.
challenges.valid_limit_note: If clouds erase the shadow, record that condition rather than estimating a position.

challenges.title: 20-minute meteor count
challenges.summary: Count all meteor-like streaks seen during one timed naked-eye observing interval without assigning shower membership.
steps: From a safe permitted night site, note start time and broad sky conditions.
Watch a wide area of sky with unaided eyes for 20 minutes.
Record the count and any interruptions or cloud/light limits; do not classify shower membership.
safety: Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: A count of zero is valid data and must not be treated as failure.

challenges.title: Horizon map
challenges.summary: Draw the skyline and major obstructions from one safe permitted observing spot without storing coordinates.
steps: Choose a stationary safe place you are already allowed to use.
Sketch the horizon line and obvious obstructions such as buildings or trees.
Label broad directions only if you already know them; do not record precise coordinates.
safety: Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: The goal is a usable local sketch, not a survey-grade map.

challenges.title: Twilight transition log
challenges.summary: After the Sun is no longer visible, record how the sky and first visible lights or stars change over a short interval.
steps: Begin only after the Sun is no longer visible from your location.
Every five minutes, record a short note about sky brightness and what becomes visible.
Stop before conditions or location become unsafe.
safety: Do not use this challenge for direct solar viewing or to stare near the Sun.
Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: Cloud or artificial light can be recorded as part of the observation.

challenges.title: Moon versus landmark comparison
challenges.summary: On two safe opportunities, sketch the Moon's apparent position relative to a distant fixed landmark.
steps: From one stationary safe place, choose a distant fixed landmark.
Sketch the Moon and landmark together when both are visible.
Repeat on another opportunity and compare apparent position; do not infer distance from the sketch.
safety: Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: If the Moon or landmark is not visible, record that limitation and try another safe opportunity.

challenges.title: Wide-sky naked-eye scan
challenges.summary: Scan a broad part of the night sky with unaided eyes and record three visual patterns or brightness differences.
steps: Let your eyes settle in a safe dark-enough place without walking around while looking up.
Scan broadly rather than fixing on one target.
Record three patterns, brightness differences, or uncertainties; names are optional.
safety: Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: Object identification is optional; descriptive observation is the goal.

challenges.title: Apparent sky-motion sketch
challenges.summary: From one stationary safe place, sketch a bright pattern, wait, then sketch it again relative to the horizon.
steps: Choose a bright pattern and a fixed horizon reference.
Make a first simple sketch.
Remain in the same safe place and make a second sketch later, then compare apparent movement.
safety: Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: If clouds interrupt the second sketch, preserve the first and record the interruption.

challenges.title: Dark-adaptation comparison
challenges.summary: Compare what you notice immediately after arriving with what you notice after a short period away from bright light.
steps: From a stationary safe place, record what is visible at first glance.
Avoid bright screens for 10–15 minutes while remaining stationary.
Record what additional faint detail, if any, becomes noticeable.
safety: Do not walk around in darkness while dark-adapting; remain in a known safe stationary place.
Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: No improvement is a valid result, especially under cloud or strong local lighting.

challenges.title: Moon light-and-dark sketch
challenges.summary: Make a naked-eye sketch of broad bright and dark regions on the Moon without requiring feature identification.
steps: When the Moon is comfortably visible, observe it with unaided eyes.
Sketch only broad bright/dark regions and the illuminated outline.
Add cloud, glare, or visibility notes; feature names are optional.
safety: Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: A rough sketch is enough; the activity does not test drawing quality or feature naming.

challenges.title: Repeat and compare
challenges.summary: Repeat any prior safe challenge and document what changed, what stayed similar, and what remains uncertain.
challenges.duration_label: Use the duration of the chosen prior challenge
steps: Choose one earlier challenge that is safe and practical now.
Repeat its observation without changing the original record.
Write three notes: changed, similar, uncertain.
safety: Use only a permitted, stationary observing place; do not observe from roads, driveways with moving traffic, drop-offs, or water edges.
If an unfamiliar night site is needed, scout it in daylight first and stop if conditions feel unsafe.
challenges.valid_limit_note: Different weather or visibility is part of the comparison rather than a reason to discard the attempt.

activities.title: Paper planisphere
activities.age_guidance: Suggested for learners who can safely use scissors and follow printed assembly instructions; adult help is appropriate for younger learners.
activities.skill_guidance: Beginner sky orientation and paper assembly.
materials: Two sheets of paper or thin card
steps: Open the reviewed latitude-specific planisphere generator.
Choose a kit for the latitude nearest your observing location; do not enter a precise address into Lumina.
Print all pieces at the same scale and follow the external assembly instructions.
Use the assembled planisphere as an approximate sky-orientation aid.
safety: Use scissors and hole-making tools carefully; younger learners should have adult help.
Do not use a conventional planisphere as a navigation or emergency-safety tool.
activities.learning_objective: Relate time, date, latitude, and the changing set of constellations above the horizon.
activities.expected_observation: The viewing window changes as the wheel is rotated, showing different sky regions for different times and dates.
activities.cleanup: Store the paper/card wheel flat and put away scissors and fasteners.
activities.adult_supervision_note: Adult assistance is recommended for cutting or punching holes when appropriate.
limitations: There is no universal planisphere: the chart depends on latitude.
Conventional planispheres are a poor fit very near the equator; use an appropriate interactive sky map there.
Lumina links to the external generator and does not redistribute its printable kit.

activities.title: Pinhole projector
activities.age_guidance: Suitable with adult supervision whenever cutting or solar-safety judgment is involved.
materials: Two pieces of stiff card or a box
Scissors if making a box version
steps: Make a small pinhole in foil or card according to the reviewed indirect-projection method.
Stand with the Sun behind you so you are facing away from it.
Project the image onto white paper or the inside surface of the box.
Adjust the distance between pinhole and screen while continuing to face away from the Sun.
safety: Never look at the Sun through the pinhole.
Never look directly at the Sun as part of this activity.
Do not combine the pinhole with binoculars, telescopes, camera lenses, or other concentrating optics.
Adult supervision is required for children and for cutting/punching steps.
activities.learning_objective: Observe how a small aperture can project an image without direct viewing of the light source.
activities.expected_observation: A small projected image of the Sun appears on the screen when geometry and lighting are suitable.
activities.cleanup: Put away pins/scissors safely and recycle or store card/foil materials.
activities.adult_supervision_note: Adult supervision is strongly recommended because this is a solar activity and may involve sharp tools.
limitations: This is indirect projection only, not a solar-viewing filter.

activities.title: Moon-phase model
activities.age_guidance: Suitable for school-age learners and adults; younger learners may benefit from adult help with setup.
activities.skill_guidance: Beginner spatial reasoning with light and a simple sphere.
materials: Small white ball or foam sphere
Pencil or stick to hold the sphere
Single lamp in a dim room
steps: Use the lamp as the Sun and hold the white ball at arm's length as the Moon.
Keep your head as the observing Earth position and slowly move the ball around you.
Observe how the illuminated fraction facing you changes while half of the ball remains lit by the lamp.
Compare the pattern with NASA's reviewed Moon-phase explanation.
safety: Use a cool, stable household lamp and keep materials away from hot bulbs or flames.
Move slowly and keep the floor clear while rotating.
activities.learning_objective: Model how changing Sun-Earth-Moon geometry produces the observed sequence of lunar phases.
activities.expected_observation: The visible illuminated portion changes as the model Moon moves around the observer even though the lamp always lights half the sphere.
activities.cleanup: Switch off the lamp and store the sphere and holder.
activities.adult_supervision_note: Adult help is appropriate when selecting or positioning a lamp for younger learners.
limitations: The tabletop model is not to physical scale and does not reproduce orbital inclination or eclipse frequency.

activities.title: Simple spectroscope
activities.age_guidance: Best for learners able to use scissors safely; adult help is appropriate for younger learners.
materials: Diffraction grating material from a safe classroom kit
steps: Build the simple viewing body using the reviewed NASA activity as guidance.
Use only ordinary household/artificial light sources that are safe to look toward normally.
Compare the patterns produced by two or more different safe artificial light sources.
Record colors/bands as observations rather than trying to identify chemical composition in v1.
safety: Never point the spectroscope at the Sun.
Never look at the Sun directly or through this spectroscope, binoculars, telescopes, cameras, or other optics.
Do not use lasers, flames, ultraviolet lamps, or damaged electrical fixtures as light sources.
Use scissors carefully and request adult help when appropriate.
activities.learning_objective: Observe that different light sources can produce different distributions of visible wavelengths.
activities.expected_observation: Different safe artificial light sources may show continuous-looking color bands or more discrete bright bands.
activities.cleanup: Switch off test lights when finished and store the spectroscope and tools.
activities.adult_supervision_note: Adult help is recommended for construction and selection of safe light sources when appropriate.
limitations: This activity is qualitative and does not calibrate wavelength or identify materials conclusively.

activities.title: Scale Solar System
activities.age_guidance: Suitable for learners comfortable measuring lengths; younger learners may need adult help.
steps: Choose either a distance-focused or size-focused scale rather than mixing incompatible scales.
Use the reviewed NASA/JPL values or worksheet to place markers consistently.
Compare spacing in the inner and outer Solar System.
Record which distances surprised you and which model limitations remain.
safety: If using a long floor or outdoor model, keep the line away from roads, stairs, doorways, and trip hazards.
Do not place stakes or markers where they could injure someone or damage property.
activities.learning_objective: Understand the extreme scale differences in Solar System distances and/or sizes.
activities.expected_observation: A consistent scale makes the outer-planet spacing much larger than many intuitive drawings suggest.
activities.cleanup: Remove all tape, string, beads, chalk, or temporary markers and leave the area as found.
activities.adult_supervision_note: Adult help is appropriate for long outdoor layouts or small materials around young children.
limitations: One compact model generally cannot show both planetary sizes and orbital distances accurately at the same physical scale.

activities.title: Shadow tracking
activities.age_guidance: Suitable for school-age learners and adults with a safe outdoor observation area.
activities.duration_label: Three or more checks across 1–3 hours
materials: Stable upright object or pencil in modeling clay
steps: Place or choose a stable upright marker in a safe sunny area.
Without looking at the Sun, mark the end of its shadow.
Repeat after at least 30 minutes two or more times.
Compare changes in shadow direction and length.
safety: Never stare at or deliberately look toward the Sun; observe only the shadow.
Keep the marker and observation area out of roads, walkways, and other trip hazards.
Use removable markings and obtain permission before marking shared surfaces.
activities.learning_objective: Connect the changing shadow of a fixed object with the Sun's apparent motion caused by Earth's rotation.
activities.expected_observation: The shadow tip changes position and often length over time when direct sunlight is available.
activities.cleanup: Remove temporary markers and return the observation area to its original condition.
activities.adult_supervision_note: Adult supervision is appropriate for younger learners outdoors or where site hazards are possible.
limitations: Clouds and surrounding obstructions can prevent useful shadow measurements; this is a valid limitation.

activities.title: Meteor counts
activities.age_guidance: Suitable for learners who can safely remain at a permitted night observing site; minors should participate with a responsible adult.
activities.skill_guidance: Beginner timed observation and record keeping.
activities.duration_label: 20 minutes plus optional 10–20 minutes of dark adaptation
materials: Optional reclining chair or blanket appropriate for the site
steps: Choose a permitted safe observing site and note broad sky/cloud/light conditions.
Remain stationary, look at a broad area of sky with unaided eyes, and count meteor-like streaks for 20 minutes.
Record the total count and interruptions.
Do not assign shower membership unless you are using a separate validated observing method.
safety: Scout unfamiliar observing terrain in daylight and avoid roads, drop-offs, water edges, isolated unsafe areas, and other hazards.
Do not walk around while looking up or while dark-adapted.
Dress for conditions and stop if weather, wildlife, security, or visibility makes the site unsafe.
activities.learning_objective: Practice a fixed-duration observational count and document conditions that affect what was seen.
activities.expected_observation: The count may be zero or more; visibility depends on sky conditions, local light, Moonlight, and natural meteor activity.
activities.cleanup: Pack out all materials and leave the site as found.
activities.adult_supervision_note: Minors should participate with a responsible adult; all users should follow local site rules and personal-safety guidance.
limitations: A simple count is not a calibrated meteor-shower rate and does not establish shower membership.
